head: 14bac80
target: A repo opts into the push gate with a tracked .own-your-diff marker instead of machine-local core.hooksPath. install writes the hook into the clone, and sync keeps a PATH copy of the gate so every opted-in clone gets gated.
incidental: selftest moved from skills/own-your-diff/scripts/ to scripts/, unchanged
SKILL.md and the usage text now describe install and sync
agent-mode.md wording: spawn each examiner fresh, with none of your context

questions.prompt: Why does the repo now opt in by committing a .own-your-diff file, instead of setting core.hooksPath to a .githooks dir carried in the tree?

options.label: Every clone sees the opt-in, because the marker is tracked. core.hooksPath lived only in the clone where it was set.
Git ignores core.hooksPath during a push, so the old gate never ran.
The gate needs a tracked file to find its ledger under .git.
core.hooksPath cannot point at a directory inside the repository.

key_points: core.hooksPath is local config: it stayed in one clone and did not travel to fresh clones
the marker is tracked, so the opt-in travels with every clone and a session hook can install the gate wherever the marker is
the tree no longer carries a .githooks dir; the only gate artifact in the tree is the marker

questions.prompt: An opted-in repo is cloned. What does its tracked tree carry from the gate, and where do the other pieces live?

options.label: The tree carries only the marker. The hook lives in each clone's hooks dir, and the gate runs from outside the repo.
The tree carries the marker and the pre-push hook, as the old .githooks design did.
The tree carries the marker, the hook, and a copy of the gate.
The tree carries only the marker, and git downloads the hook from the plugin at push time.

key_points: the only gate artifact in the tracked tree is the marker
the hook is per-clone state, written into that clone's hooks dir, and never tracked
the gate binary lives outside the repo, at a stable location on the user's PATH

questions.prompt: The pre-push hook runs, but it cannot find quizgate anywhere. What happens to the push, and why?

options.label: The push is blocked, with a message that says where to get the gate. A missing gate must not let unquizzed work through.
The push goes through, because a missing gate is not the author's fault.
The hook asks the author to pass the quiz before the push continues.
The push goes through, and the hook notes the missing gate for the next sync.

key_points: the hook fails closed: it blocks the push and exits nonzero
the message points the author to where the gate comes from
the reason: a hooked clone must not push unquizzed work just because the gate went missing

questions.prompt: A teammate clones an opted-in repo on a fresh machine. Nothing has installed a hook in that clone yet. She pushes unquizzed work. Which of these hold?

options.label: The clone has the marker but no pre-push hook, because the hooks dir never travels with a clone.
Git blocks the push, because the marker tells git that pushes need a quiz.
The push goes through, so the gate covers a clone only after install or sync has run there.
Running quizgate install in that clone would write the hook and close the gap.

key_points: the hooks dir is per-clone and never travels with the repo
git never reads the marker; the marker alone gates nothing
coverage in a clone comes from install or sync having run there
install closes the gap for that clone by writing the hook

questions.prompt: quizgate install runs in a clone that already has the author's own pre-push hook. What does it do?

options.label: It refuses to touch the file, and prints the one line the author must add.
It backs the file up and puts its own hook in its place.
It appends its own check to the end of the file.
It skips the clone silently and waits for the next sync.

key_points: the write path never overwrites a hook the author already has
it fails loudly and says which line to add so the author keeps control
a hook that already belongs to the gate is left alone

questions.prompt: install and sync now do different jobs. In your own words: what is each job, and who runs it?
key_points: install is the one-time opt-in: the author runs it once per repo, and it writes the marker to commit and the hook in that clone
sync is the recurring path: the plugin's session hook runs it, and it refreshes a stable copy of the gate on the user's PATH and quietly installs the hook in any opted-in clone that lacks one
the stable PATH copy exists because the plugin's install dir moves with updates, and the hook needs a place that does not move
the cost: the PATH copy can lag behind the real gate until the next sync

questions.prompt: A team opts a repo in and commits the marker. One teammate works with the plugin for a day. Another uses plain git, with no plugin, and pushes unquizzed work in her first hour. Which of these are true?

options.label: The plugin teammate gets the hook from sync, without ever running install, and an unquizzed push is blocked.
The plain-git teammate's push goes through: her clone has the marker but no hook, and git never reads the marker.
Both teammates must set core.hooksPath before any push is gated.
Sync commits the marker in the plain-git teammate's clone, so her next push is blocked.

key_points: the marker is tracked, so it arrives with every clone, and it gates nothing by itself
sync installs the hook in opted-in clones, so plugin users are covered with no per-clone install
a plain git user has no hook until she runs install herself; the gate leans on the plugin for coverage
core.hooksPath is gone from the flow
